2027-02-02.title: Mayaltho · The Entrance of our Lord into the Temple
readings: The Spirit rests on the shoot of Jesse
Christ entered the Holy Place with his own blood
2027-02-02.alt: Mayaltho, the Entrance of our Lord into the Temple (2 February), forty days after Yaldo.
2027-02-02.verse: Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation.
theo: Forty days after his birth, Mary and Joseph bring the Child to the Temple “to present him to the Lord”, as the Law required for every firstborn son, and they offer the sacrifice of the poor: “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons” (Leviticus 12:8). The Lord of the Temple enters his own house, carried in his mother's arms. Malachi had promised: “the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple” (Malachi 3:1).

There an old man, Simeon, “righteous and devout, looking forward to the consolation of Israel”, takes the Child in his arms and praises God: “Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel.” A whole life of waiting is fulfilled in one embrace.

Then Simeon says to Mary: “This child is destined for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be opposed… and a sword will pierce your own soul too.” Joy and sorrow meet at the Temple door. The Child presented today will offer himself on the Cross. Hebrews says: Christ “entered once for all into the Holy Place, not with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own blood, thus obtaining eternal redemption.”

Mayaltho comes just before the Great Fast. It teaches us to present our lives to God, as Mary and Joseph presented Jesus; to wait faithfully like Simeon and Anna; and to welcome Christ, the light of the nations, into our arms and our hearts.
conn: The Lord comes to his Temple.
Malachi 3:1 is fulfilled: the Lord enters his Temple, not in power but as a child.
Leviticus 12:8: the Holy Family offered two birds, the gift of those who could not afford a lamb. The true Lamb was in Mary's arms.
Leviticus 22:17–25 requires offerings without blemish; Christ is the spotless offering (1 Peter 1:19; Hebrews 9:14).
Simeon's song echoes Isaiah 42:6 and 49:6: the Servant is “a light to the nations”.
altar: Simeon held the Lord in his arms; in Holy Communion we receive him into our hearts. Simeon's song is a fitting prayer after Communion: “Now, Lord, let your servant go in peace; my eyes have seen your salvation.”
outline: Forty days after Yaldo the Child comes to the Temple.
Mary and Joseph give their Son to God. Do we offer our children and our lives?
Faithful waiting in old age; the elderly as witnesses of hope.
Joy and sorrow together: the Child is the sign that will be opposed.
Present yourself to God as Lent begins.
live: Begin each morning this week by presenting your day to God.
Visit an elderly person and listen to their memories of faith, as Simeon and Anna would have shared theirs.
Pray Luke 2:29–32 each night before sleep.
fathers: “Let us all hasten to meet him… let us all carry lights… Simeon took him in his arms; let us too embrace him” (Sermon on the Hypapante).
He marvels that the Lord of the Temple was carried into the Temple, and that the old man held the Ancient of Days, who released him in peace (Hymns on the Nativity).
magis: The presentation of Jesus in the Temple shows him to be the firstborn Son who belongs to the Lord; Simeon and Anna recognise in him the long-expected Messiah.
Jesus showed deep respect for the Temple, where he was presented forty days after his birth.
The feast of the Presentation is kept in the universal Church as the World Day for Consecrated Life.
saints: 3 Feb: Mar Simon and Morth Hanna (Simeon and Anna). 4 Feb: St John de Britto. 7 Feb: Kothine Sunday; the Great Fast begins.
2027-02-02.prayer: Lord God, your Son was presented in the Temple and received by Simeon and Anna. Accept the offering of our lives; let us wait for you with their faith and welcome you with their joy, and let your Christ be the light of our homes and of all nations. Amen.

quick: The Lord enters his Temple in Mary's arms.
Simeon: “My eyes have seen your salvation.”
Joy and the sword: the Child will give himself for us.
2027-02-02.action: Present your day to God each morning this week.
2027-02-02.question: Have I presented my life, my family and my work to God?
2027-02-02.special: Mayaltho, the Entrance of our Lord into the Temple. World Day for Consecrated Life in the universal Church.
illus: Old Kerala grandmothers often say: “I only want to see my grandchildren baptised and receive Holy Communion, then the Lord can take me.” That is Simeon's prayer, prayed in every generation.

family.explain: When Jesus was a baby, Mary and Joseph took him to the Temple. An old man called Simeon held him and was so happy, because he had waited all his life to see the Saviour.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and all elderly people, and for sisters, brothers and priests who have given their lives to God.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we offer our family to God this week?”

kidsaint: Two very old people who prayed in the Temple every day, waiting for the Saviour. God let them see baby Jesus before they died. Lesson: keep praying and waiting for God; he keeps his promises.
term: Syriac for “entrance”: the feast of the Entrance of our Lord into the Temple, 2 February, forty days after Yaldo. In the West it is called the Presentation of the Lord.
termMore: Luke 2:29–32, “Now, Lord, let your servant go in peace”, is prayed in many Christian traditions at night prayer, at the end of the day.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, forty days after Yaldo, Mary and Joseph carry the Child to the Temple in Jerusalem. They come to present him to the Lord, as the Law of Moses required, and they offer two young pigeons, the offering of poor families. The Lord of the Temple enters his own house, carried in his mother's arms.

An old man is waiting there: Simeon, righteous and devout, who had been promised that he would not die before seeing the Messiah. He takes the Child in his arms and sings: “Now, Lord, you are letting your servant go in peace, for my eyes have seen your salvation.” A whole lifetime of prayer is rewarded in one moment. And the old prophetess Anna gives thanks and speaks of the Child to everyone.

But Simeon also says to Mary: “A sword will pierce your own soul too.” The Child presented today will one day offer himself on the Cross. Hebrews tells us that Christ entered the true Holy Place with his own blood, obtaining eternal redemption. The joy of Christmas already carries the shadow of the Cross.

On Sunday the Great Fast begins. Let us do what Mary and Joseph did: present ourselves to God, our families, our work, our whole life. Let us learn from Simeon and Anna to wait for the Lord faithfully. And every time we receive Holy Communion, let us say with Simeon: “My eyes have seen your salvation.” Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus was a tiny baby, Mary and Joseph took him to the big Temple to give him to God.
An old man called Simeon was there. He had waited all his life to see the Saviour. He held baby Jesus in his arms and said: “Now I am happy; I have seen God's salvation!”
When you receive Jesus or pray to him, you can be happy like Simeon. Let's say: “Jesus, you are my light!”

intro: Theme: “The Lord comes to his Temple.”
Forty days after his birth, Mary and Joseph bring Jesus to the Temple. There two elderly people, Simeon and Anna, recognise him. The Lord whom Israel sought has come to his house.

sub: The Law allowed those who could not afford a lamb to offer two birds.
Mary and Joseph bring the offering of the poor; yet they carry the true Lamb.
God values not the size of our gift but the heart that offers it.
q: If she cannot afford a sheep, she shall take two turtledoves or two pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering.
They offered a sacrifice according to what is stated in the law of the Lord, “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”
points.apply: Offer yourself, your family and your work at the altar today, however small it seems.

sub: Malachi promised: the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.
Simeon, righteous and devout, waited for the consolation of Israel; the Spirit led him to the Child.
Holding Jesus, he sings: now I can depart in peace. Faithful old age sees salvation.
q: The Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.

Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel.
points.apply: Honour the elderly in your family and parish; listen to their faith.

points.h: A sign that will be opposed
sub: Isaiah spoke of a stone of stumbling as well as a sanctuary.
Simeon tells Mary that the Child will be a sign opposed, and a sword will pierce her soul.
Following Christ means choosing a side; Mary shows us how to stand faithful in sorrow.
q: He will become a sanctuary, a stone one strikes against; for both houses of Israel he will become a rock one stumbles over.

This child is destined for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be opposed so that the inner thoughts of many will be revealed—and a sword will pierce your own soul too.
points.apply: Ask Mary for courage to remain faithful to Christ when it costs you.

concl: The Light of the nations entered the Temple in the arms of his mother.
Let us receive him as Simeon did, and let our lives be an offering in his house.
2027-02-02.resolve: Pray Simeon's song (Luke 2:29–32) each night before sleep this week.
